target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: fix(chat): preserve explicit current-source sends in Control UI history
target.body:
Related: #104544
Related: #83494

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could explicitly send a successful `message` tool reply to the exact current source conversation, while Control UI history omitted that delivered reply and showed only a later, different assistant final.

This PR addresses the explicit current-source `message` send slice of #104544. It does not address missing subagent lifecycle announcements, which are tracked separately in #105517.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit routes were excluded from message-tool history projection even when the resolved channel, account, target, and thread matched the current source conversation. The change adds a structured current-source route marker at the outbound owner and permits marker-backed successful explicit sends in the history projector.

Dry-run, suppressed, and explicit `ok: false` results remain excluded. Existing transcript delivery mirrors remain authoritative and are deduplicated.

## User Impact

Users who receive an explicit agent reply in the current Telegram/Slack source conversation can now see the same reply in Control UI session history. Later assistant output no longer replaces that delivered message in the dashboard.

Cross-channel, cross-account, cross-target, and cross-thread sends remain excluded from the current session history.

## Evidence

- Exact patch head: `ccceb3f971e24022effe1b170a217edf618761ff`
- Exact replay base: `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`
- Current exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29249860500 (passed)
- Current exact-head fork patch CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29249860584 (passed)
- Current upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29249852157 (passed)
- Previous exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29246179834 (passed at `f89cdc7b510268a9cd76c7e66c44784f8afe4bc7`)
- Previous exact-head upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29242075130 (passed at `5ca0701495e263fe78a784d270ca7d154ecdcfe4`)

The branch was replayed without patch-content changes onto upstream `main` at `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`. A commit-by-commit range comparison matched all seven patch commits. The prior exact-head failures reproduced on the corresponding upstream baseline and were outside this PR's nine changed files: dangling msteams symbols, generated locale inventory drift, a plugin SDK baseline hash, and an asynchronous SQLite reliability helper mismatch. All of those upstream failures are repaired in this replay base. Upstream `main` has since advanced only in files outside this PR's nine-file surface, so another replay is not needed for this evidence cycle.

The exact-head Control UI workflow passed and produced the expected artifact. Upstream PR CI and fork patch CI also passed against the refreshed patch: the upstream workflow tested the merge result, while the fork workflow pinned the exact patch SHA.

## Risk And Rollback

Risk is limited to read-time history projection and the structured result metadata used to prove an exact current-source route. The marker is emitted only after trusted channel/account/target/thread resolution, and projection continues to reject existing non-success indicators.

Rollback is a straight revert of this PR. No config, schema, transcript migration, or persisted data rewrite is introduced.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed. This restores consistency between an existing channel delivery path and the existing Control UI history surface without changing configuration or user-facing commands.
